subject.title: Feature: temp artifact provenance + durable-path guardrails to prevent /tmp chaos

question: What scope should OpenClaw core own for temp artifact provenance and runtime-critical temp path guardrails?
rationale: The request is valid safety work, but implementing it requires choosing storage ownership, cleanup semantics, and whether janitor-style artifact classification belongs in core, plugin APIs, or a ClawHub/plugin workflow.

options.title: Core guardrails first
options.body: Implement core doctor/runtime validation for post-reboot-critical temp-backed paths and design provenance APIs separately for plugin or later core adoption.

options.title: Core provenance registry
options.body: Add a SQLite-backed core temp artifact registry with scratch/reproducible/durable classes and janitor semantics in one broader product change.

options.title: Narrow to concrete bugs
options.body: Keep only specific runtime temp-path failures and cleanup bugs open, and leave general janitor provenance to plugins or user SOPs.

recommendation.title: Core guardrails first
recommendation.body: Implement core doctor/runtime validation for post-reboot-critical temp-backed paths and design provenance APIs separately for plugin or later core adoption.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest available history around filesystem safety, temp guardrails, and the related plugin-vs-core scope decision.
